newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Legal & General may reach 850p.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Legal & General may reach 850p.

text.p: DAY'S RANGE * SUPPORT * RESTNCE* MA-25 * MA-200

+ Chart breakout from 740p by Legal & General shares indicates the continuation of a long-term bull trend begun in 1995. After overcoming resistance at 815p, the shares could then reach 850p, technical analysts said.
+ Turnover in the shares has increased following the breakout and the completion of a continuation head-and-shoulders pattern confirm the positive stance on the stock.
Recent chart breakout on high volume by shares in life insurer Legal & General suggest the stock price may run up towards 850p, after negotiating initial resistance at 815p, technical analysts said.
"The stock has made a clean break on the price-relative chart and from 740p on the absolute price chart," said Nick Glydon, technical analyst at Robert Fleming Securities.

By 0750 GMT, the shares were down 1/2 to 793-1/2p. They embarked on a long-term bull trend in 1995, from a low of 415p in January that year, and over the past nine months they have shuffled sideways between 665p and 740p, noted Glydon.

Turnover in the shares had declined over the summer months but picked up smartly as the shares broke-out. This implies the extent of investor interest in the shares and a likelihood that more buyers will be attracted to the shares fuelling further price rises.
Breakout from 740p may have completed a particular chart pattern which is rarely seen, said Glydon.
This is a continuation head-and-shoulders pattern, in which the share price first traces out three distinct troughs following an uptrend.
The pattern is completed by an upward break from a line connecting the two peaks within the pattern so that the original upward trend can continue.

Legal & General's price-relative chart -- of the share price divided by the All-Share index -- is now at a 12-month high, implying further outperformance for the shares against the general market, said Glydon.
"The shares are still in a long-term uptrend," he added.
